concerns.text: Spectral-residual salience is computed from the Fourier amplitude spectrum of the grayscale image — i.e., it is mathematically a function of the same low-level luminance/contrast statistics entered as covariates (FR-009). Regressing salience on outcomes while 'controlling for' its own inputs risks over-adjustment/attenuation and makes the covariate-adjusted coefficient hard to interpret. The plan should state this limitation and report both covariate-adjusted and unadjusted salience effects.

No center-bias control. Spectral-residual and center-surround saliency maps both have strong central peaks, and eye-tracking fixations are also strongly center-biased; this shared bias can produce a spurious salience–dwell association — a canonical confound in this literature. Add an explicit control (e.g., center-of-image distance covariate or annulus-based baseline comparison).

first_fixation_prob is a binary event per trial (first fixation lands in ROI or not), yet Model A is a linear MixedLM treating it as a continuous DV. A logistic GLMM (or per-participant/ROI aggregation with weights) is the appropriate link for this outcome; the plan only mentions log-transform/Gamma for dwell time.
